citation: Lloyd, C., Edovald, T., Kiss, Z., Morris, S., Skipp, A., & Ahmed, H. (NatCen Social Research) (2015). Paired Reading: Evaluation report and Executive summary. London: Education Endowment Foundation. (Programme developed/delivered by Allen Thurston & Maria Cockerill, 2013; cited in the meta-analysis as 'Thurston 2016'.)
report_number: EEF project: Paired Reading (peer tutoring), July 2015. ERIC ED581127.
design: Cluster RCT; assignment at CLASS level (not school) within schools, with schools modelled as fixed effects; 10 secondary schools in NE England (North/South Tyneside & Sunderland); 120 classes (58 intervention, 62 control); 2,736 pupils (1,370 Year 7 tutees aged 11-12; 1,366 Year 9 tutors aged 13-14). Intervention = Paired Reading peer-tutoring programme over 16 weeks (20 min/week); teachers trained by the delivery team with manual + digital resources (the TPD component). Subject = reading/literacy (NGRT). Grades = Mixed (Year 7 & Year 9 / KS3). Low SES context.
problems: (1) Authorship/year: the meta-analysis labels this 'Thurston 2016', but the EEF report was independently evaluated by NatCen Social Research (Lloyd et al.) and published July 2015. Allen Thurston (with Cockerill) is the PROGRAMME DEVELOPER/deliverer (Thurston & Cockerill, 2013), which is almost certainly why the meta-analysis keyed it to him; intervention attributes (peer-tutoring/cooperation, external trainer, long duration, teacher training = TPD, Low SES, Mixed grade) all match registry row 123. Confident this is the correct report. (2) Assignment level: registry says 'School' but the report randomised at CLASS level within schools (schools as fixed effects); the cluster unit for the effect size is therefore the class, with class-level ICCs reported. n_clusters recorded as 120 classes (60 per year-group analysis). (3) The report's 'effect size' is computed per Tymms (2004) = (adjusted multilevel impact coefficient on age-standardised score) / (pupil-level SD from an UNADJUSTED multilevel model). It is pretest-adjusted and model-based (class random intercept + school fixed effects), so cluster_adjusted=true. It is NOT formally Hedges' g (no small-sample J correction applied by the report), but it is the standardized mean difference the meta-analysis would have used; g fields hold the report's effect size, g_method documents this. (4) impact_se derived from the reported 95% CI of the effect size (width/3.92); g_var = g_se^2. (5) All outcomes are reading/literacy -> Reading. The primary outcome (NGRT Overall Reading) is the headline; the two secondary outcomes (Passage Comprehension, Sentence Completion) are the two components/subscales of the Overall Reading scale (outcome_role=subscale). (6) Year 7 pupils are TUTEES (receive reading help); Year 9 pupils are TUTORS; both are in the intervention -> treated as two grade samples, both full-sample. (7) NGRT is standardized/independent (GL Assessment), but testing was administered by schools so EEF reduced its padlock security rating to 4; test_type kept standardized_independent. (8) FSM primary-outcome rows included as pre-specified subgroups (is_full_sample=false). Gender subgroups not extracted as separate rows (noted only). Overall: no evidence of impact; all effects small/negative.

effect_sizes.g_method: Report's effect size (Table 12, adjusted) = Tymms(2004): adjusted multilevel impact on age-standardised reading score (-0.28) / pupil-level SD from unadjusted multilevel model = -0.02.
